newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says foreigners in lost plane presumed dead.
newsitem.headline: Peru says foreigners in lost plane presumed dead.

text.p: An American and two Canadian men whose plane disappeared over Peru's dense eastern Amazon jungle on Friday were presumed dead, rescuers said on Monday.
"Frankly, I don't think we'll find any survivors," said Oscar Salvador, an air force spokesman in Pucallpa where the twin-motor Cessna C-404 went missing.
The plane, belonging to Canadian airline Aerodat, was being used by U.S. oil company Anadarko Petroleum Corp.
Salvador said since Saturday a Peruvian air force helicopter and plane have been searching the area where the Cessna was believed to have disappeared "but without positive results up to now."
He said bad weather and difficult terrain were hindering the search and added: "It's a hostile zone without any chance for an emergency landing."
Pucallpa airport officials identified the missing men as pilot Kent Widmer and oil engineers Pierre Moisan, both from Canada, and Clifford Bishop from the United States.
